headline: COPPER RECORD: $6.67/lb surge mints 23 new billion-dollar "unicorn" mines in one year
snippet: With copper touching a record $6.71/lb intraday and sustaining near $6.67/lb, Mining.com calculates that 75 mines now generate over $1 billion annually in copper revenue alone — 23 more than the previous tally. The surge is fundamentally repricing copper mine economics and accelerating M&A interest across the sector.

headline: BIPARTISAN SILVER ACT: Senate bill would force geographic spread of U.S. precious metals vaults beyond New York
snippet: Senators Risch (R-ID) and Cortez Masto (D-NV) introduced the bipartisan SILVER Act requiring COMEX-approved depositories in each U.S. time zone, addressing national security risks from concentrating precious metals storage near New York. Money Metals CEO Stefan Gleason is part of the broad industry coalition backing the bill.

headline: ATHABASCA URANIUM HUNT: Skyharbour commences first drilling at RL project alongside Denison joint venture
snippet: Skyharbour Resources (TSX-V: SYH) mobilized crews to begin 4,000–5,000 metres of diamond drilling at the South Russell target of its RL uranium project in Saskatchewan's eastern Athabasca Basin. The program follows a ground EM survey and marks the first drill test of the highest-priority targets at the project.

headline: AMERICAS GOLD swaps 592k oz Sprott silver stream for shares, cutting $45M in future debt
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver (TSX: USA) agreed to terminate its remaining 592,000-ounce silver delivery obligation to Sprott Mining Inc. by issuing 7.96 million shares at a deemed price of US$5.57, eliminating over $45 million in variable future liabilities and increasing shareholders' direct leverage to silver prices.

headline: SCOTTIE RESOURCES launches 52,000-meter drill campaign near Stewart, BC — biggest in company history
snippet: Scottie Resources (TSX-V: SCOT) kicked off a 52,000-metre drill program at its namesake property 32 km north of Stewart, British Columbia, focused on upgrading and expanding resources to support a potential direct-shipping ore (DSO) mine. The program is the largest in the company's history.

headline: TURNING POINT: Sovereign bond yields breaking multi-decade highs as foreign central banks dump U.S. Treasuries
snippet: Global sovereign bond yields are breaching multi-decade resistance as foreign central banks reduce U.S. Treasury exposure, driven by rising debt service costs and improving domestic yields. The structural shift creates a short-term headwind for gold while reinforcing the long-term case for hard assets as fiscal risks escalate.

headline: HONG KONG targets July launch of government-backed gold clearing system to rival London and New York
snippet: Hong Kong's government-owned precious metals central clearing company is targeting trial operations in July 2026, aiming to build a third global gold pricing hub. The Airport Authority has set a 2,000-tonne gold storage target within three years, and the new infrastructure is expected to accelerate Asia's role in physical gold price discovery.

headline: AGNICO EAGLE doubles Wallbridge Mining stake to near 20% with C$22.4M private placement
snippet: Agnico Eagle (TSX/NYSE: AEM) invested C$22.4 million to purchase 243.9 million Wallbridge Mining shares at C$0.092 each, lifting its stake from 9.9% to nearly 20%. Agnico cited high geological potential as the rationale — a move the market typically reads as the prelude to a buyout offer.

headline: CHINA SOFTENS on rare earth controls after Trump-Xi summit — pledges cooperation but keeps export regime intact
snippet: Following the May 14–15 Trump-Xi summit in Beijing, China pledged to address U.S. concerns about yttrium, scandium, neodymium, and indium shortages — but analysts at Benchmark Minerals say the export control regime is structurally intact and will remain Beijing's key strategic leverage. Phase 2 controls stay suspended until November 2026.

headline: GOLD AT $4,500 FLOOR — But analysts say the looming bond crisis could change everything for precious metals
snippet: Gold is struggling to sustain the $4,500 handle as rising bond yields and a firm dollar weigh on sentiment, but multiple analysts argue that a sovereign bond crisis — driven by fiscal deficits and foreign Treasury selling — could trigger a fundamentally different wave of safe-haven demand that bypasses traditional gold headwinds.
